items.title: Procter & Gamble vs. Colgate-Palmolive: Which Dividend Stock Is Safer?
items.summary: Both consumer giants beat earnings, yet their margins are moving in opposite directions as oil prices climb and a cautious U.S. shopper holds back. One dividend carries a thin balance sheet buffer, and retirees need to know which one.

items.title: General Mills Just Gained 15% in a Month: Take Profits, or Buy More?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysGeneral Mills is up 15% in the past month, lifted by Procter & Gamble’s and Kraft Heinz’s quarterly reports while tech stocks sold off. General Mills had no news of its own behind the move, and Campbell’s ran even further.

items.title: 3 Dependable Dividend Stocks for a $250,000 Passive Income Strategy
items.summary: One of these dividend payers slashed its quarterly check in 2022, and another has a stock that has gone nowhere in five years. Why would a retiree still trust them with a third of a $250,000 income plan?

items.title: 3 Dependable Dividend Stocks for a $250,000 Passive Income Strategy
items.summary: Three household names have raised their payouts for more than 60 straight years, yet each one yields less than REITs or BDCs. So why do they anchor a $250,000 income plan, and which one pays the most?

items.title: Coca-Cola Is Up 39% This Year. How Much of That Is Earnings and How Much Is Multiple?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysCoca-Cola stock is up 39% this year, and the midterm rally sent it, Procter & Gamble and Colgate-Palmolive toward 52-week highs. Roughly three-quarters of Coca-Cola’s gain came from investors paying a higher multiple, and only about a quarter from higher earnings estimates.

items.title: Is Wall Street Bullish or Bearish on Procter & Gamble Stock?
items.summary: Procter & Gamble has outpaced the broader market over the past year, and analysts remain moderately bullish about the stock’s prospects.

items.title: Here’s Why Dividend Kings Coca-Cola, Procter & Gamble, and Colgate-Palmolive Are Hitting 52-Week Highs Following Midterm Election Results
items.summary: Investors are piling into dependable dividend stocks following the midterm elections. But after their latest rallies, are these three Dividend Kings still worth buying?

items.title: Walmart's Dec. 11 Dividend Isn't the Real Reason to Own the Stock
items.summary: Walmart won't offer much in terms of income, but its ability to boost dividend payouts for 53 consecutive years shows the strength of its business model.
